title: LCARS theming for the command buffer split and surrounding chrome
description: The nvim command buffer panel and its surrounding kitty split should look like part of the LCARS interface — consistent with the existing prompt theming. This may involve changes to the existing zsh prompt, the kitty tab/border styling, or nvim statusline. Goal is visual coherence: the command area reads as an LCARS panel, not a bare terminal.
notes: Added laststatus=0 to nvim launch -c flags in kitty/lcarcat.keybindings.conf. Both tabline and statusline are now suppressed in the command buffer split. Deployed and ready to validate.

title: Auto-resize nvim command panel as content grows beyond minimum lines
description: When the nvim buffer content exceeds a minimum line threshold (e.g. 2 lines), dynamically expand the bottom panel and shrink the panels above it. Shrink back when content decreases. Use kitty's resize-window action or a hook in nvim's TextChanged event to trigger the resize.

title: Keybinding to submit nvim buffer content as shell command
description: Implement the submit flow: a keybinding (e.g. <leader>Enter or a kitty shortcut) reads the nvim buffer content, sends it to a designated shell panel via kitty's send-text or kitten, and optionally clears the buffer. Must handle multi-line commands correctly.
design: Submit keybinding sends buffer content to the kitty pane directly above the command buffer. Default behavior: keep the submitted command in the buffer (do not clear). A separate 'send and clear' variant may be added later. Multi-line commands must be handled correctly. The existing lcarcat-z2g bead covers appending to a history file.

title: Pin nvim command buffer panel to bottom of kitty layout
description: Create a persistent kitty panel (horizontal split at bottom) that runs an nvim instance configured as a command input buffer. The panel should appear on a keybinding, stay pinned, and not interfere with the primary work panels above it. Configure nvim to start in insert mode with a single scratch buffer for command input.
design: Mode is opt-in: user launches the command buffer mode explicitly (keybinding TBD). On entry, the kitty window gets a horizontal split at the bottom running an nvim instance; the existing shell scrollback stays above. Panel is persistent for the duration of the mode session. In a single-window layout, one nvim buffer appears below the shell. In a two-split side-by-side layout, each split gets its own nvim command buffer below it. The nvim instance loads the full user config (some features may be hidden/disabled later). Mode exit is deferred to a future bead.
notes: Implemented as ctrl+a>b in kitty/lcarcat.keybindings.conf. Uses launch --location=hsplit --bias=20 (4-line starting height). Nvim launched with buftype=nofile bufhidden=hide noswapfile and startinsert. File is now deployed via deploy.sh and included from kitty.conf.
close_reason: Implemented ctrl+a>b in kitty/lcarcat.keybindings.conf (launch --location=hsplit --bias=6, nvim scratch buffer in insert mode). File added to deploy.sh mappings and included from kitty.conf. Validated live — panel opens at ~4 rows.

title: NVIM command buffer panel: replace readline with full editor in kitty
description: Replace the readline/zsh vi-mode command input with a dedicated nvim instance pinned to the bottom of the kitty layout. The nvim buffer provides full syntax highlighting, linting, and editing capabilities. A keybinding submits the buffer content as a command to a shell panel. The panel auto-resizes as content grows, and integrates with zsh history for incremental search.

title: Switch prompt bar images to kitty Unicode placeholder cells
description: The elbow and cap images are drawn as kitty Unicode placeholder cells (U+10EEEE + row/col diacritics) rather than cursor-anchored a=T placements. Placeholder cells live in the text stream and scroll with the bar on resize, fixing the dangling elbow in scrollback. Images are transmitted once per session with U=1 virtual placements and reused across prompts.

title: Incremental backwards search over zsh history in nvim command buffer
description: Provide access to zsh history (both session history and ~/.zsh_history global file) from the nvim command buffer. Implement incremental backwards search (like Ctrl-R) using a telescope or fzf picker that populates the buffer with the selected history entry. Should feel as fast as shell Ctrl-R.

title: Capture submitted commands to lcarcat history panel
description: After a command is submitted from the nvim buffer to the shell panel, capture that command and append it to the lcarcat history pane. This feeds the existing history display so submitted commands appear in the LCARS-styled history log, not just in the shell's own history.

title: Add AWS profile chip to LCARS zsh prompt
description: Render a chip showing the active AWS_PROFILE alias in the lcars swoop prompt. Red when it matches a prod alias (dep); AWS-orange otherwise. Shown only when AWS_PROFILE is set. Also add to the plain non-graphics fallback prompt.

Switchable by include-ing it from kitty.conf after the base colorscheme.

title: Split resize reflows stale swoop images
description: Opening/closing a vsplit reflows the pane, but the elbow/cap PNGs already drawn on previous prompts don't move with their now-shifted text: kitty graphics placed with a=T are anchored to a cursor cell at draw time, not re-laid-out on resize, so old bars end up with elbows/caps in the wrong columns until those lines scroll away. The current prompt redraws correctly on the next prompt (pane detection refreshes on SIGWINCH); only scrollback history is affected. May not be cheaply fixable — options: clear/redraw graphics on WINCH, use unicode placeholders, or accept it. Related to lcarcat-2m7.3 (nvim: anchor the prompt swoops the same way) — same windowless/transmit-once fix.
notes: Fix: replaced cursor-anchored (a=T) elbow/cap placement with kitty Unicode placeholders (U+10EEEE + rowcolumn diacritics). Images transmitted once per shell with fixed ids (1 elbow-L, 2 elbow-R, 3 cap-L, 4 cap-R) and a virtual placement (U=1), sized in cells; placeholder cells live in the text stream so they reflow/scroll with their bar on pane resize instead of dangling. Only the 2 bar rows (grid rows 0-1) are drawn as placeholders; the elbow's 3rd grid row (stem stub + inner fillet) is dropped and the left stem is redrawn as a plain periwinkle PROMPT cell (also reflow-safe, and more on-design per minimum-viable-image). Tradeoff: sub-cell inner fillet on the input line is gone. New helpers _lc_ph/_lc_transmit/_lcars_transmit_images in zsh/prompt_lcars.zsh; deployed to ~/.config. Verified: syntax + emitted byte streams correct. STILL NEEDS live-kitty visual confirmation (reload prompt, open/close a vsplit, check scrollback bars track their text).

title: nvim image chrome
description: LCARS image chrome for nvim: kitty-image elbows/caps drawn by image.nvim as windowless absolute-screen images. Outer-frame model with top-left/bottom-left elbows on the leftmost gutter, rounded caps for gutterless windows, capped-channel horizontal separators. Shipped in nvim/lua/lcars/chrome.lua (opt-in :LcarsCorner), assets regenerate at physical cell size cached by <cellw>x<cellh>-<gutter>. This epic tracks remaining chrome polish and robustness work.

title: Full-screen nvim command mode: three-panel layout with history, nvim buffer, and scrollback
description: A full-screen mode integrating lcarcat-cwl history panel, the nvim command buffer, and a shell scrollback region into a single kitty layout. Layout order and proportions are TBD. This is a future design exploration once the basic per-split nvim command buffer (lcarcat-08g) is stable.

title: Handle interactive full-screen CLI apps launched from nvim command buffer
description: When the user submits a command from the nvim command buffer that opens a full-screen interactive application (e.g. launching nvim, htop, or a TUI), the kitty layout needs to handle the takeover gracefully — either suspending the command buffer panel or routing the application to the correct window. Behavior is undefined until the basic command buffer epic (lcarcat-08g) is stable.

title: Elbow-swoop tab-bar integration + tagbar color rework
description: Merge the panel visually with the tab bar via an elbow swoop, and rework the tab-bar colors so they coexist with the elbow swoop. Depends on the surface decision from the panel spike.

title: Recall command to the prompt line
description: Populate the shell input line with a selected previous command from the history, so it can be edited/re-run. A definite requirement.

title: Scrollback fold/minimize: right cap
description: The right cap of a pill collapses/minimizes that command's output in the terminal window. Exploratory — keep decision-gated on whether folding feels good (see the panel spike).

title: Navigate: left cap scrolls command + scrollback to top
description: The left cap of a pill scrolls that command and its scrollback to the top of the terminal output window, driven via scroll_to_prompt / kitty @ remote control targeting the entry's OSC 133 mark.

title: Pill buttons for history entries
description: Render each history entry as a vertical-line pill in LCARS chrome, with the two caps as distinct actions (left = scroll-to-top, right = fold/minimize). Reuse the _LC_* palette and the prompt's chip patterns. Handle selection highlight and list scrolling.

title: History data layer
description: Implement the chosen capture mechanism (from the capture spike) into a persistent per-window store: command text, cwd, exit code, duration (from $_LCARS_START), STARDATE/timestamp, and the scrollback position / OSC 133 mark. Keyed by $KITTY_WINDOW_ID; the panel reads it. This is the data layer the sidebar renders.

title: Spike: panel surface & interaction model
description: Prototype the panel surface and interaction: overlay-over-window (launch --type=overlay) vs a real kitty pane that reflows the other tabs. Try a couple of interaction styles so Seth can pick a preference. Also evaluate whether scrollback folding feels good here. Deliverable: a decision on surface + interaction model.

title: Spike: command-capture mechanism
description: Prototype and compare three ways to capture per-command history for the sidebar: (a) a per-window scratch file under ~/.local/kitty/tmp cleaned up on kitty quit / next launch, (b) echoing the command into scrollback, (c) fetching it from scrollback via the OSC 133 marks kitty already emits. Deliverable: a decision on which mechanism feeds the data layer, with notes on tradeoffs (persistence, robustness, cleanliness).

title: History navigation sidebar
description: An LCARS-styled side panel listing the session's past commands, letting you browse and jump to any one in the terminal's scrollback. Builds on the OSC 133 prompt marks kitty shell-integration already emits and the scroll_to_prompt binds in kitty/keybindings.snippet.conf. The prompt (zsh/prompt_lcars.zsh) already runs preexec/precmd hooks that know each command's text, start time ($_LCARS_START), exit code, and STARDATE — this epic extends that capture into a browsable, navigable history overlay.
design: Architecture sketch: (1) preexec/precmd records per-command metadata (command text, cwd, exit, duration, stardate, and the scrollback line/mark) into a per-window store. (2) A kitty overlay window (launch --type=overlay) or kitten panel renders the list in LCARS chrome. (3) Selecting an entry drives navigation in the underlying window via scroll_to_prompt / kitty @ remote control to land on that prompt's OSC 133 mark. Reuses the existing OSC 133 marks and _LC_* palette; keep everything opt-in behind $LCARS like the rest of the toolkit.

Raw Unicode placeholders (demos/placeholder_preview.py) are the alternative for cells we fully control, but they do NOT render inside nvim's own tabline/statusline strings.

Key the placement by id, skip re-render when geometry/asset is unchanged, and delete stale ids. See kitty graphics-protocol docs on displaying one image at multiple locations.
